And this production is a pristine piece of work, unmissable for anyone who cares about this monumental playwright.
Druid has done a fine job exploring Beckett’s mysteries, and if you want to see him done well, head off-Broadway.
This production perfectly captures Beckett’s unique mixture of guffaws and the grotesque, unlike the lightweight all-star Broadway Waiting for Godot now on Broadway.
As comparisons are supposedly odious, none will be made here as to the varying successes of the three, other than to say they each had notably strong aspects.
Allowing them the humanity of discontent, let alone dissent, works against the piece, and suddenly we’re just watching four people vainly complain for 90 minutes.
The Druid Theatre production of Samuel Beckett’s Endgame runs at the Irish Arts Center (726 Eleventh Ave.) through Nov. 23.
Endgame, as delivered by Druid at the Irish Arts Center, resonates.

cn.t: Garry Hynes' acclaimed production finds fresh laughs and urgent relevance in Beckett's apocalyptic classic, with most critics praising the ensemble's grasp of absurdist humor and the brutalist design, though one finds it lacks grounding compared to recent revivals.
